answer: Agents stake a walnut-shaped bond in the ridge; the bond’s nut cracks during 12-hour time-locked proofs audited by a rotating tundra jury. A Sybil needs fresh 12-hour proofs per identity, costing 12 hours of tundra jury time per head, because the ridge sets each proof’s start exactly at the jury’s cycle boundary and won’t batch across heads in the same cycle.
